hero.subtitle: Wrocław Tech and TU Graz students explore the world of semiconductors in a Unite! Seed Fund project that combines education, hands-on experience and international exchange.

silicon.intro_body: Common sand contains a lot of silicon dioxide (SiO₂). But it's not pure enough for electronics. The journey begins by extracting and refining silicon from quartz sand through a high-temperature chemical process - a requirement for creating reliable microchips.
silicon.step1_body: Silicon sand contains a lot of silicon dioxide (SiO₂). The journey begins by extracting and refining silicon from quartz sand through a high-temperature process - a requirement for creating reliable microchips. Silicon is purified to 99.9999999% (nine nines) purity.
silicon.step2_body: The ultra-pure silicon is melted and grown into a single large crystal using a process called the Czochralski method. A seed is shaped into a cylindrical ingot - a perfect silicon structure that forms the base for every modern microchip.
silicon.step3_body: The silicon ingot is sliced into thin wafers, like microscopic pancakes. Each wafer is polished to atomic-level smoothness, creating a flat surface ready for circuit printing. These wafers are now ready for microchip design.
silicon.step4_body: Photolithography transfers the circuit pattern onto the wafer using light. Layer by layer, transistors are built at nanometer scale - smaller than a virus. A single modern chip contains billions of transistors.
silicon.step5_body: Each chip is cut from the wafer, tested for defects, and packaged into the familiar black chips we know. From raw sand to finished processor - the journey of silicon is complete.

stats.section_subtitle: In 2023, the European Union passed the EU Chips Act - a landmark regulation to secure Europe's semiconductor supply chain, reduce strategic dependencies, and make Europe a global leader in chip technology by 2030.
stats.stat1_label: in public and private investment mobilised by 2030
stats.stat2_label: target share of global chip production - up from ~9% today
stats.stat3_label: target year for doubling Europe's share of world chip output
stats.stat4_label: Europe's current share of global semiconductor production
stats.project_link: Our project embraced this ambition directly - bringing engineering students face-to-face with chip fabs, clean rooms, and research labs to broaden awareness of semiconductors as a strategic industry.
stats.source_note: Source: European Commission — EU Chips Act, 2023

exchange.section_subtitle: Two student communities. Two countries. One shared passion for technology.
exchange.graz_body: Members of KN Solvro visited Graz - the Silicon Valley of Europe. They toured ams OSRAM's production facilities including a Clean Room, explored Silicon Austria Labs' cutting-edge research, and visited laboratories at Technische Universität Graz. The Austrian students from BEST Graz ensured the visit combined technical depth with cultural warmth.
exchange.wroclaw_body: TU Graz students visited Wrocław, hosted by KN Solvro. They explored XTPL's nanoprinting technology, Balluff's sensor solutions, and the Wrocław Centre for Networking and Supercomputing (WCSS). The programme also included a tour of the Faculty of Electronics at Wrocław Tech, including the specialist Clean Room, organized with the NaMi student research group.

about.section_subtitle: The two student organisations behind the project.
about.solvro_university: Wrocław University of Science and Technology
about.solvro_desc: The biggest IT student organization of its kind in Poland. Based at WUST, but with international impact - we build apps from students to students, push the boundaries of science through AI/ML research, and foster community by running events that empower the next generation of skilled engineers.
about.best_desc: A student organisation at TU Graz with 20 active members, dedicated to connecting students with industry and academia through international events and career fairs.
